Reality.rationale: The problem is grounded in an identifiable robotics and soft-contact control setting: continuous rigid-probe sliding/scanning over compliant finite-area environments. The declared evidence context covers finite-area ultrasound MPC, geometry/distributed-pressure/friction MPC, low-order viscoelastic tissue force control, PFC, force-uncertainty MPC, model-agnostic wrench admittance, and finite-area viscoelastic mechanics, which together make the proposed operating conditions and contact-information variables physically and experimentally real rather than speculative.

Importance.rationale: The question targets whether richer contact representations improve impedance choices and held-out closed-loop outcomes, not merely model fit. That matters because the evidence context indicates active but fragmented prior work across memoryless learned impedance, finite-area MPC, friction/contact geometry, uncertainty-aware MPC, and wrench admittance; resolving minimal sufficient representations would guide sensing, modeling, and controller design choices under practical scanning conditions.

Unresolvedness.rationale: The packet explicitly positions the candidate against prior work that handles related pieces separately: memoryless learned impedance, finite-area MPC, geometry/distributed-pressure/friction MPC, low-order viscoelastic force control, PFC, force-uncertainty MPC, model-agnostic wrench admittance, and finite-area mechanics. The candidate asks for operating-condition-specific incremental value and minimality of contact representations under held-out closed-loop outcomes, which is not already settled by those strands individually.

Precision.rationale: The scope is bounded to rigid-probe continuous sliding/scanning over compliant finite-area environments and explicitly names the compared representations, baselines, held-out operating conditions, outcomes, exclusions, and proposed study family. The wording avoids universal and clinical claims and asks for condition-specific minimal sufficient representations.

Falsifiability.rationale: The falsifier is explicit: richer contact components fail to matter if simple baselines select equivalent impedance and match richer forms within prespecified margins on held-out transient wrench/force, constraint violations, contact loss/slip, and independent scanning-quality outcomes. The minimality claim is also testable through observability, reproducibility, and incremental prediction requirements.

Answerability.rationale: The proposed randomized repeated-measures phantom study, with withheld specimens and variation over relaxation, stiffness, thickness/curvature, contact-area changes, speed, direction, dwell, tangential load, and disturbances, provides a plausible route to answering the question. Equalizing data, compute, objectives, and safety across nested representations directly supports attribution of any improvement to the added contact information.
